prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a close-up indoor scene by an angled window frame, with the camera wearer's right hand at the bottom right (~0.2–0.4 m away) holding a dark glossy balloon or ornament (~0.3–0.5 m away, right-of-center) within arm's reach. To the left (~0.4–0.7 m away, ~0.2–0.3 m left of the dark object) are green and pink paper flower decorations, a white cup at the bottom-left edge in frames 4–5, and triangular bunting flags hanging above them in front of the window mullion (~0.5–0.8 m away). Across the five frames, the camera tilts slightly downward and leftward while the right hand and dark object remain at a steady foreground distance, partially occluding the lower window frame and background decorations. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map clearly separates the foreground silhouette of the dark glossy object and hanging bunting planes from the window sash behind them, which is otherwise complicated by specular reflections and transparency in RGB. However, the depth map is unreliable across the glass panes (rendering distant outdoor trees and reflections at inconsistent mid-range depths in frames 4–5) and fluctuates in brightness on the lower-left green flower between frame 1 (very bright/near) and frames 4–5 (darker/farther).
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the foreground dark object in the lower-center/right (~0.3–0.5 m from the camera wearer) and the camera wearer's right hand entering from the lower-right edge (~0.2–0.4 m away, within arm's reach and touching the dark object's right side). It also detects a small yellow bottle at the top-left corner behind the window glass (~0.7–1.0 m away, above and ~0.5 m left of the dark object) in frames 3–5, and a partially visible cup at the bottom-left edge (~0.4 m away) in frame 5. Across the five frames, the hand mask moves slightly inward from the right edge in frames 1–3, disappears in frame 4 as the hand shifts further out of view, and reappears in frame 5, while the cup mask emerges at the bottom left as the camera pans slightly down and left. This map highlights the small top-left bottle and bottom-left cup rim that are easily overlooked amidst the cluttered decorations in the RGB strip. However, the segmentation map is highly unreliable on the foreground dark object—misclassifying it as a 'person' facing no actual direction in frames 1, 2, and 5, missing it completely in frame 3, and mislabeling it as a 'cat' in frame 4—while failing to segment the bunting flags and paper flowers entirely.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is almost entirely blank across the sequence, showing no valid human bodies looking toward or away from the camera wearer, nor any magenta hand skeletons for the camera wearer's visible right hand at the bottom right (~0.2–0.4 m away, within arm's reach). In frames 2 and 3 only, a spurious yellow shoulder-and-facial-keypoint cluster appears near the bottom center (~0.3–0.5 m in front of the camera wearer) superimposed on the lower portion of the dark foreground object, oriented roughly parallel to the image plane. From frame 1 to frame 5, this false skeleton appears in frame 2, shifts slightly upward and narrows in frame 3 as the camera and hand move slightly, and vanishes completely in frames 4 and 5. The pose map adds no valid spatial information beyond the RGB image because the only actual human body part present—the partially occluded right hand at the lower-right edge—is completely missed across all five frames. It is entirely unreliable here, hallucinating a person's upper torso and head keypoints on the curved, glossy black surface of an inanimate foreground object in frames 2 and 3.
